residual_risks: INFERRED: the fallback (two-call) client treats a reply with an EMPTY/absent response.url as answered in place (only `redirected===true` or a URL that differs from the request URL is rejected). Rationale: iOS RCTNetworking always reports response.URL.absoluteString and whatwg-fetch copies xhr.responseURL, so on device a redirect surfaces as a different URL; URL-less replies only come from the base-pinned test stand-ins in __tests__/wf/*. The durable path's fetchNoRedirect remains strict (empty URL = redirected). Operation-id binding still guards a URL-less {deleted:true} reply whenever the request named an operation.

INFERRED: if the server's delete-request reply omits operationId (production supabase/functions/api always includes it), the fallback confirmation is unbound (pre-existing base-pinned contract in accountDeletion.test.ts); the durable path never accepts such a request reply.

The fallback client is still reachable when the local SQLite database cannot be opened; it journals nothing, so a confirmation whose reply is lost cannot be resumed after the dialog closes (the dialog shows the honest unknown state until closed). Removing the fallback entirely would break base-pinned suites outside write_paths.
Apple runtime behaviour (real device redirect handling) is not verified here — Linux/Jest only; no Mac runner used per package rules.
implement.summary: Defects on BASE_SHA 5c1859a8 (INFERRED from code, VERIFIED by the new suite failing 25/26 there): apps/mobile/src/screens/ManageAccountScreen.tsx calls requestAccountDeletion/confirmAccountDeletion directly over plain globalThis.fetch (no journal, no operation binding, no redirect rejection; `confirmDeletion` re-arms the challenge on retryable errors), and apps/mobile/src/account/deletion.ts:~230/~262 default `fetchFn = globalThis.fetch` and accept any 200 {deleted:true}. The r2 candidate had wired the durable foundation but left two adversary breaks: A1 — ManageAccountScreen.runStep re-checked apiSessionForDeletion(context) AFTER foundation.confirm() returned confirm_unknown, and the confirm fallback was the ARMED step, so an owner change during an in-flight confirmation rendered 'Delete your account?' + enabled 'Permanently delete' + 'Keep my account' over a confirm_pending row; A3 — with getDb() throwing, accountDeletionFlow() fell back to legacyAccountDeletionFlow over plain fetch, accepting a redirected 200 {deleted:true} as 'Account deleted' and running the local purge. Fix (commit f8ce1d44, on top of test commit 1e02480e): (1) runStep performs the owner/session check exactly once before the step is handed to the flow and shows whatever the flow reports afterwards; the fallback now receives `sent` and a confirmation that was already sent fails into confirm_unknown ('Deletion status unknown', Retry deletion/Close, ACCOUNT_DELETION_UNKNOWN_MESSAGE) — never a re-armed challenge; completionUnknown/timers are set consistently in the catch path. (2) The two-call client (only reachable when the local DB cannot be opened or cannot host the journal) now defaults to `fetchInPlace`: redirect:'error', credentials:'omit', cache:'no-store', referrerPolicy:'no-referrer', and a reply whose reported URL differs from the request URL (or redirected===true) is dropped before its body is read; requestAccountDeletion captures the server's operationId and confirmAccountDeletion sends {challenge, operationId} and refuses a {deleted:true} reply that does not name that operation. The adversary's A3b reply (url https://attacker.example/..., deleted:true) therefore renders as the unknown outcome and completeAccountDeletion is never called; a redirected step-1 reply renders 'Nothing was deleted' and arms nothing. The durable path (deletionOperation + deletionOperationTransport via fetchNoRedirect, journal resume, idempotent re-entry, receipt-gated purge) is reused from r2 unchanged. Legacy exports keep their signatures (string challenge still accepted) so the base-pinned suites accountDeletion.test.ts, manageAccountScreen.test.tsx, wf/flow-account-deletion.test.tsx and wf/flow-offline-network-errors.screens.test.tsx pass unmodified; the full mobile suite is green (6090 passed).
